newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble dips on dollar buying but slowed by c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Rouble dips on dollar buying but slowed by c.bank.

text.p: The rouble eased on Tuesday as banks found it attractive to invest excessive rouble funds in dollars, dealers said.
They said the central bank's bid/offer rates were making the rouble's fall much slower than it might have been given the low overnight credit rates.
"Commercial banks are seeing the dollar higher than the central bank's rates, which are restricting the market," an Interbank Finance House dealer said.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,441-42 per dollar compared with an early 5,436-39. Deals were not struck on Monday due to the U.S. Columbus Day holiday. Russian banks use U.S. counterparties for settlement.
Tomorrow roubles eased to 5,439-40 per dollar from Monday's late 5,434-36.
The central bank said it had set 5,429/5,439 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Tuesday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded two to five percent compared with Monday's late zero to five percent.
One dealer said the low cost of rouble funds had made dollar investments more attractive.
"Dollar today rates are so high because there are no other good ways of investing them, while dollar buying is yielding five percent in hard currency," he said.
Dealers said Treasury bill auctions to be held on Wednesday failed to boost rouble demand, as usually happens on Mondays and Tuesdays.
On Wednesday, October 16, the central bank is auctioning 7.5 trillion roubles of six-month paper and three trillion roubles of an additional tranche of three-month bills.
